m.aarti.tek: Hear, my Goddess, this Tuesday's worship: we stand at your door with joined hands. Taking betel leaf, areca nut, a flag and a coconut, we lay our offering before you, O Jvālā. Hear us, Mother of the world, do not delay; you fill the storehouses of the saints. Protector of the saints, ever bringing well-being: Mother, victory to Kālī, who brings about good.
m.aarti.pad1: You are the giver of understanding, the Mother of the world: accomplish my task. I have taken shelter at your lotus feet and have come to your refuge. Whenever trouble has fallen on the devotees, each time you have come to their help.
m.aarti.pad2: Again and again you have enchanted the whole world, taking on the matchless form of a young woman. As a mother you play with your son; elsewhere, as a wife, you enjoy pleasures. You give joy to the saints and are ever their helper; the saints stand and hail your victory.
m.aarti.pad3: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, with the thousand-hooded Śeṣa, stand at your door to give their offerings. My Mother sits on an unshakeable throne, and a golden canopy turns above her head. On Saturday your hue is of kumkum, when you give your command to Luṅkaṛ, your attendant Lāṅgur.
m.aarti.pad4: With sword, skull-bowl and trident in your hands, you burn Raktabīja to ashes, slay Śumbha and Niśumbha in a moment, and seize Mahiṣāsura and crush him. On Sunday, O primal Bhavānī, you take away the suffering of your own devotee.
m.aarti.pad5: Enraged, you slay the dānavas and crush Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa and all of them. When you look on in your merciful form, you remove trouble in an instant. You have taken on a gentle nature, my Mother, and you grant your devotee's plea.
m.aarti.pad6: The glory of the seven days has been told; who can tell all your virtues? Bhavānī, mounted on the lion's back, reigns in her unshakeable abode. Devotees receive your darśana and sing songs of blessing; siddhas and seekers lay their offerings before you.
m.aarti.pad7: Brahmā reads the Vedas at your door, and Śiva meditates. Indra and Kṛṣṇa perform your āratī, and Kubera is waving the fly-whisk. Victory to the Mother, victory to Mother Bhavānī, who reigns in her immovable abode.
